findings.F1: The whole loss of the book comes from shorts still held after the coin's 30-day return had turned positive. Shorts held while the regime was still "mean_reversion" (30-day return below 0) earned +4.43 in summed bar gains over 10,304 bars. Shorts carried into the "unknown" regime lost -6.55 over 3,374 bars. The book's total is -2.11 before about 1.76 of fees.
findings.F2: Being short in the wrong place is what loses, not the signal itself. On the bars the book was short, the coin's mean next-day return was -0.023 %. On flat bars it was +0.242 %. Bars in the unknown regime lost about 0.19 % each at a mean short size of 0.79. In those bars the coins were rising about 0.25 % a day, roughly 2.5 % over 10 days, which is larger than the idea's whole unusual move of +1.79 %.
findings.F3: The idea is real but thin once the drift is counted. Per case, the unusual move is +1.79 % (strength 0.098), while the coin's normal drift against the short is -1.38 %. The total move is only +0.41 %, 1.8 times the 0.22 % round trip. Any loss from holding past the move wipes it out.
findings.F4: Holding runs past the idea's 10-day horizon, and those extra days lose. The 2,229 short trades lasted 11.3 days on average, with a mean gross of -3.38 %, a net of -3.49 % and 35 % winners. The 595 trades lasting 10 to 20 days lost a mean of -4.35 % to -6.18 % net. The case-level total move over exactly 10 days is +0.41 %.
findings.F5: Trades also fire often relative to the edge. There were 2,362 fresh-break bars, and the forecast sat at -20 on more than half of them (median -20). That gave 0.056 trades per day, at fees summing to 1.76 against a gross of -2.11. The cost is a second burden on a small total move, not the main cause, which is F1.

ideas.idea: When a coin closes above a price where it turned down several times in the past 90 days while its 30-day return is negative, it tends to fall back over the next 10 days, and the deeper its 30-day decline, the larger the fall, only while its 30-day return is still negative on each of those days; the fall is largest when the 30-day return stays deeply negative through the 10 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader fading a break of a repeatedly-held high in a falling month should hold the fade only as long as the month is still down, and drop it as soon as the coin's 30-day return turns positive.
ideas.name: false break while month falls

ideas.idea: When a coin's 30-day return turns from negative to positive, the coin rises over the next 10 days, and the larger its new 30-day return, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader should refuse to be short a coin whose 30-day return has just turned positive, and may lean long in proportion to the size of the turn.
ideas.name: monthly turn up continues

ideas.idea: When a coin closes above a price where it turned down several times in the past 90 days while its 30-day return is negative, it tends to fall back over the next 10 days, and the deeper its 30-day decline, the larger the fall, with most of the fall inside the first 10 days and a rise after them.
ideas.consequence: A trader fading such a break should close the fade at its 10-day horizon rather than carry it, because the days after the horizon give the move back.
ideas.name: false break fades within horizon
